Vendorcumproprietor Serial number of the case : 02/0814 Date of the commission of the offence : 14/07/2007 Date of filing of the complaint : 02/01/2008 Cc No. 02/08 Da Vs. Pradeep Bansal Page 1 of 9 Name of the Complainant : Sh. Sanjiv Kumar Gupta, Food Inspector Offence complained of or proved : Section 2 (ix) (k) of Pfa Act 1954 r/w Rule 32 of Pfa Rules 1955 1955 punishable U/s 16 (1) (a) r/w section 7 of the Pfa Act. Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty Da vs . Pradeep Bansal Page 1 Of 9 on 10 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15169949/ 1 Final order : Acquitted Arguments heard on : 10/09/2015 Judgment announced on : 10/09/2015 Brief facts of the case 1. In brief the case of the prosecution is that on 14.07.2007 at about 12:30 p.m, Food Inspector Sanjiv Kumar Gupta and Field Assistant Sh. Brahma Nand under the supervision and directions of Sdm / Lha Sh. Manoj Diwedi visited the premises of M/s Bansal Store, S. No. 29, Cscii, Sector09, Rohini, Delhi110085 , where accused Pradeep Bansal who was the vendor cum proprietor was found present conducting the business of various food articles including Haldi Powder, for sale for human consumption and in compliance of the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as the Act & Rules) the Food Inspector collected / purchased the sample of Haldi Powder. 2. It is further the prosecution's case that the sample was sent to Public Analyst for analysis and as per the report of Public Analyst the sample was found misbranded because there was complete violation of Rule 32. However Haldi Powder conformed to the standards and accordingly after obtaining the necessary Sanction / Consent under Section 20 of the Act the present complaint was filed for violation of provisions of Section 2 (ix) (k) of Pfa Act 1954 r/w Rule 32 of Pfa Rules 1955 which is punishable U/s 16(1) (a) r/w section 7 of the Pfa Act. 3. After the complaint was filed, the accused was summoned vide order dated 02.01.2008. 4. Notice for violation of provision of Section 2 (ix) (k) of Pfa Act 1954 r/w Rule 32 of Pfa Rules 1955 punishable U/s 16(1) (a) r/w section 7 of the Pfa Act was served upon the accused vide order dated 01.06.2009 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 5. The complainant/prosecution examined three witnesses i.e. Sh. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta Food Inspector as Pw1, Sh. Brahma Nand Fa as Pw2 and the then Sdm /Lha Sh. M.K. Dwivedi as Pw3 and thereafter Pe was closed vide orders dated 08.11.2013. 6. Statement of the accused U/s 313 Cr. P.C. was recorded on 27.01.2014 wherein the accused claimed himself to be innocent. Despite opportunity given the accused did not lead any defence evidence. A brief scrutiny of the evidence recorded in the matter is as under: 7. Pw1 Sh. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta deposed that on 14.07.2007 he along with Sh. Brahma Nand, Fa and other staff under the supervision and direction of Sdm /Lha Sh. Manoj Divedi visited the premises of M/s Bansal Store, Shop No. 29, Csc II,Sector 9, Rohini, Delhi where accused Pradeep Bansal was found conducting the business of the shop including Haldi Powder in sealed polythene packet bearing no label declaration, a food article for human consumption for sale. Despite opportunity given the accused did not lead any defence evidence. A brief scrutiny of the evidence recorded in the matter is as under: 7. Pw1 Sh. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta deposed that on 14.07.2007 he along with Sh. Brahma Nand, Fa and other staff under the supervision and direction of Sdm /Lha Sh. Manoj Divedi visited the premises of M/s Bansal Store, Shop No. 29, Csc II,Sector 9, Rohini, Delhi where accused Pradeep Bansal was found conducting the business of the shop including Haldi Powder in sealed polythene packet bearing no label declaration, a food article for human consumption for sale. He deposed that Da vs . Pradeep Bansal Page 1 Of 9 on 10 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15169949/ 2 he disclosed his identity and intention for purchasing the sample of Haldi Powder ready for sale in the form of sealed polythene packets having no label declaration as per selection and direction of Sdm /Lha, for analysis to which accused agreed. He deposed that before taking the sample he tried his best to procure some public witnesses by requesting some neighboring shopkeepers, customers and passersby etc to join the sample proceedings but as none agreed for the same, on his request Fa Brahma Nand agreed and joined as witness. He deposed that at about 12:30 pm, he purchased 9 X100 gms sealed packets of Haldi Powder having no label declaration on payment of Rs. 72/ vide vendor's receipt Ex. Pw1/A. He deposed that he divided the sample into three equal parts by putting three originally sealed polythene packets of Haldi Powder as one counterpart and then each counterpart was separately, packed, fastened, marked, and sealed according to Pfa Act and Rules by affixing Lha Slip bearing his code number and s ignature of LHA on all the three counter parts of the sample . He deposed that then the vendor signatures were obtained on LHA Slip on each counter part of the sample in such a manner that a portion of his signature were on the wrapper as well as the LHA Slips. He deposed that Notice in Form VI Ex. PW1/B was prepared at the spot and copy of it was given to the accused as per his endorsement at portion A to A bearing his signature at point A. He deposed that vendor made endorsement at point B to B that packet of Haldi Powder were of same lot and ready for sale. He deposed that Panchnama Ex.PW1/C was prepared. He deposed that vendor also furnished his statement Ex. PW1/D that he is incharge and responsible for day to day affairs of the said shop. He deposed that all these documents Ex. PW1/A to Ex. PW1/C were read over and explained to the accused in Hindi and after understanding the same accused signed at point A, witness signed at point B and he signed at point C respectively. He deposed that the one counter part of the sample in intact condition was deposited with the PA on 16.07.2007 i.e next working day vide receipt Ex. PW1/E and a Memo VII in a sealed packed separately. He deposed that all the copies of memo in Form VII bear the seal impression with which sample were sealed. He deposed that the two counter parts of the sample along with two copies of Memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited in intact condition with the LHA on 16.07.2007 i.e. next working day vide receipt Ex. PW1/F bearing his signature at point A with the intimation that one counter part of the sample has already been deposited in intact condition with the PA. He deposed that all the copies of Memo of Form VII bore the same seal impression with which the sample in question was sealed. He deposed that the PA Report Ex. PW1/G was received according to which the sample was found misbranded for complete violation of Rule 32. He deposed that however sample of Haldi Powder conforms to the standard, as mentioned therein at portion X. He deposed that during investigation, he sent a letter Ex. PW1/H to STO, Ward No. 63 and as per its reply at portion A, no such firm was found registered with Sales Tax. He deposed that on the spot, vendor also provided the photocopies of MCD License and DL and he was found proprietor of the said shop. He deposed that then on competition of investigation, the complete case file along with all statutory documents were sent through LHA/SDM to the then Director (PFA), Sh. N. Balachandaran who after going through the case file, applied his mind and gave his consent for prosecution Ex. PW1/I which bears his signature at point A. He deposed that complaint Ex. PW1/J was filed in Court by him bearing his signatures at point A. He deposed that intimation letter Ex. PW1/K bearing the signature of SDM /LHA Sh. Ranjeet Singh at point A was sent along with the copy of PA report by registered post to accused as mentioned therein which were not received back undelivered. He deposed that the photocopy of the postal registration receipt is Da vs . Pradeep Bansal Page 1 Of 9 on 10 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15169949/ 3 Ex. PW1/L bearing the relevant entry at portion A. 8. During his cross examination he admitted that there was a policy of the department to issue warning for first violation of Rule 32 only and on the day of sampling, the policy of the department was in existence. He admitted that no previous warning was issued to the accused as per department's policy. 9. PW2 Sh. Brahma Nand, Field Assistant and PW3 Sh. M.K. Dwivedi the then SDM/LHA have deposed on the same lines as deposed by PW1 in his examination in chief.
